chunks: 1 — The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Salih ibn Isa al-Ijli narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ali narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Bukayr narrated to us. He said: 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad al-Muhalabi narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Hilal ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura.

He said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) one day, and he said: 'I saw wondrous things last night.' He said: We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what did you see? Tell us about it — may our souls, our families, and our children be your ransom.'

He said: 'I saw a man from my community — the Angel of Death had come to take his soul, and his filial piety toward his parents came and prevented it from him. I saw a man from my community upon whom the punishment of the grave had been extended — his wudu (ablution) came and prevented it from him. I saw a man from my community who had been surrounded by the devils — the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, came and delivered him from among them. I saw a man from my community panting, surrounded by the angels of punishment — his prayer (salat) came and prevented them from him. I saw a man from my community panting with thirst — every time he approached a water pond, he was turned away — then the fasting of the month of Ramadan came, gave him drink, and quenched him.'

'I saw a man from my community — the prophets were seated in circles, and every time he approached a circle he was expelled — his ritual bath from major impurity (ghusl) came, took him by the hand, and seated him beside me. I saw a man from my community — before him was darkness, behind him darkness, to his right darkness, to his left darkness, and beneath him darkness, immersed in darkness — his Hajj and Umra came, brought him out of the darkness, and led him into the light. I saw a man from my community speaking to the believers but they would not speak to him — his maintenance of family ties came and said: O assembly of believers, speak to him, for he used to maintain his family ties — so the believers spoke to him, shook his hand, and he was among them. I saw a man from my community shielding himself from the heat and sparks of the fire with his hand and face — his charity (sadaqah) came and became a shade over his head and a cover over his face. I saw a man from my community seized by the Zabaniya (guardians of Hell) from every direction — his enjoining of good and forbidding of evil came, freed him from among them, and placed him with the angels of mercy.'

'I saw a man from my community kneeling on his knees with a veil between him and the mercy of Allah — his good character came, took him by the hand, and brought him into the mercy of Allah. I saw a man from my community whose record had fallen toward his left — his fear of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, came, took his record, and placed it in his right hand. I saw a man from my community whose scales were light — his predeceased children came and made his scales heavy. (1) I saw a man from my community standing on the edge of Hell — his hope in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, came and rescued him from that. I saw a man from my community who had fallen into the Fire — his tears that he had wept out of fear of Allah came and extracted him from that. I saw a man from my community on the Bridge (Sirat) trembling like a palm frond in a day of violent wind — his good opinion of Allah came, calmed his trembling, and he proceeded across the Bridge. I saw a man from my community on the Bridge sometimes crawling, sometimes creeping, sometimes hanging on — his prayers upon me (salawat) came, stood him on his two feet, and he proceeded across the Bridge. I saw a man from my community who had reached all the gates of Paradise — every time he reached a gate it was closed before him — his sincere testimony that there is no god but Allah came, the gates were opened for him, and he entered Paradise. (1)'

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: there is no deity but Allah (shahada)

ai.seo_question: What good deeds will save a person on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: A dream vision narrated by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) in which he describes twenty men from his community, each saved in the afterlife by one virtuous deed they had performed in this life. This hadith was narrated during a gathering of the companions and serves as a powerful exhortation to practice specific acts of worship and ethical conduct. It demonstrates the Shia theological principle that deeds are personified in the afterlife, acting as intercessors for the believer. The historical context is likely a teaching session during the Prophet's Medinan period, addressed to companions who included 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura, encouraging them to prioritize the described deeds.
